title: A worker's brief says to edit or name the docs stage-back --check lists as stale before it returns
goal: the brief's staging section tells the worker that the docs `selfdoc.py stale` lists in its stage-back --check output are read and edited, or named as still correct, before it returns

run:
import sys
t = open('_tools/bl_dispatch.py', encoding='utf-8').read()
i = t.find('"## Staging copies"'); j = t.find('links = [', i)
s = t[i:j]
print('stale named in the staging section:', 'stale' in s); sys.exit(0 if i >= 0 and 'stale' in s else 1)

clauses.clause: the brief's staging section tells the worker that the docs `selfdoc.py stale` lists in its stage-back --check output are read and edited, or named as still correct, before it returns

notes: retrospective of SP-ttgcpf7o: ST-lvcvosht's worker staged .claude/agents/kb-observer.md, saw `selfdoc.py stale --since HEAD` list kb/_self/plugin.md and token-efficiency.md and "did not look into why"; stage-back then refused until the orchestrator edited both docs (14b54df0fb). The check reads the brief text because the rule is text the brief prints.
